data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The conflict dissolves if we view scientific action not as 'predicting the future' but as 'committing to a specific line of critique,' where the 'better' theory is simply the one that offers the most precise target for refutation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the agent building the bridge actually expects it not to collapse, they have slipped into induction.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the goal of action is survival/success rather than knowledge growth, this mechanism fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"This approach radicalizes Popper's falsificationism. Preference is not for the theory that will 'work' (survive), but for the theory that, if false, will reveal its falsehood most dramatically. We prefer the well-corroborated theory because it has survived hard tests, meaning it is robust enough to sustain further, even harder, tests. The 'action' is the act of testing, not the act of relying. If we must build a bridge, we use the theory that allows us to calculate the exact load limit, knowing that if it fails, we learn more than if we used a vague theory.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
